centre.how: Common centre of the traced ring ridges 2 and 3 (fitted ellipses) in the 30 m Copernicus elevation model. Wikidata Q744591 gives 21.124, -11.402 (0.8 km away) and Wikipedia 21.1147, -11.3943 (0.5 km away).

claimed.line: The Richat's rings are Plato's ringed city, 127 stades (about 23.5 km) across, with mountains to the north and the sea at the south.
claimed.who: Bright Insight (Jimmy Corsetti) 2018; earlier Sarantitis, Alexander and Rosen
claimed.evidence: Atlantis was supposedly 127 stadia, or 23 kilometers (14 miles) across, which matches a portion of the Richat. Jimmy does note that he used Google Earth to measure the distance, which may not be completely accurate.

found.line: A natural dome 40 km or more across, about 99 million years old, eroded into rock ridges; no settlement, canal or built ring has been found.
found.evidence: The circular Richat structure and its breccia core thus represent the superficial expression of a Cretaceous alkaline complex with an exceptionally well preserved hydrothermal karst infilling at its summit.

needs_sea_level.when: about 9600 BCE (Plato) or about 12,000 years ago (the video)
needs_sea_level.why: For the rings to hold sea water the Atlantic would have to stand about 420 m above today, and reach 500 km inland; the sea was then lower, not higher.
needs_sea_level.evidence: He has to imagine that this part of the Sahara was flooded by the Atlantic 12,000 years ago.

features.label: Claimed centre of the Atlantis city
features.who: George Sarantitis (and later proposers)
features.what: Proposers say the central part of the Richat is the royal island and the rings around it are Plato's rings of land and water.

position.detail: Common centre of the traced ring ridges B and C (fitted ellipses), Copernicus GLO-30. No proposer prints coordinates for a centre point; this is the centre of the structure they point to.

features.evidence: Atlantis is the name by which Plato refers to a continent, an island and an island city-state, the latter being the concentric wheel system of Richat
features.notes: Wikidata puts the structure at 21.124, -11.402 (0.8 km from this point); Wikipedia at 21.1147, -11.3943 (0.5 km). Sarantitis first published the idea in 2008 (Atlantipedia). The Plato Project FAQ is an archived 2022 copy.

features.label: Ring ridge 1: about 6 km across
features.who: Matton, Jébrak and Lee (rings described); crest line traced here from elevation data
features.what: Innermost traced ridge ring, the edge of the central depression.
features.result: About 6.0 km across (mean), 5.8 by 6.3 km as an ellipse; crest height 387-447 m. Strong ridge signal on about 80% of its length.

position.detail: Crest line traced by this lane from Copernicus GLO-30 tiles N20/N21 W012 (30 m): ridge filter (second derivative, 120 m smoothing), then the strongest connected crest per 1 degree of azimuth around the centre (dynamic programming, 3 degree output spacing). Checked by overlay on the 2024 geological map: it follows the unit boundaries.

features.evidence: Erosion has created circular cuestas represented by three nested rings dipping outward from the structure.
features.notes: Matton et al. say "three nested rings" but give no radius for each, so which of our traced ridges are their three is our reading. Ridges are rock: the strata dip outward at 10-20 degrees, there is no water in them.

features.label: Outer rim ridge: east and south arc
features.who: Matton, Jébrak and Lee (structure at least 40 km across); crest traced here
features.what: The outermost cuesta ridge, traced only where it is a clear ridge, from north-east round the east and south to the south-west.
features.result: It lies 21.5 to 24.2 km from the centre, so the structure is at least 43 km across if symmetric; crest height 364-515 m.

position.detail: Same method as the ring ridges, azimuth 45 to 230 degrees only. North and west of that the outer edge runs along the Adrar plateau escarpment, which a ridge filter cannot tell from the ring, so it is left out.

features.evidence: The Richat structure (Sahara, Mauritania) appears as a large dome at least 40 km in diameter within a Late Proterozoic to Ordovician sequence.
features.notes: Wikipedia and the IUGS site say about 40 km; the east and south arcs we traced are 21.5-24.2 km from the centre (see measurements).

features.label: Outer gabbro ring (Tin Jouker)
features.who: Matton and Jébrak; Abdeina and others
features.what: The outer of two rings of dark igneous rock (gabbro), drawn on the 2024 map as a ring about 7 km from the centre.
features.result: The 2024 paper argues the two gabbro rings are sills of about 200-230 million years old rock, not ring dykes, and not Cretaceous.

position.detail: Figure 1 of Abdeina et al. 2024 (CC BY). Control points: its printed graticule lines, one every 0.04 degrees (2 min 24 s) both ways, found at x = 242, 548, 855, 1160, 1467, 1772 px and y = 164, 491, 819, 1147, 1475 px of the 1896 x 2268 px figure, taken as lon -11.48 to -11.28 W and lat 21.20 to 21.04 N. The printed 2.5 km scale bar (183 px) gives the same scale as the grid (73.8 px/km). The corner labels are not on grid lines, so the grid lines were numbered by hand; the numbering was checked against the 30 m elevation model (south-west salt flat within 0.2 km) and ring traces. Blue line digitised by colour in 4 degree steps; a 13 degree gap in the NNE is left open.

features.evidence: The ca. 70 m-wide outer ring (Tin Jouker) is located 7–8 km from the centre, while the 30 m-wide inner one (Guelb Richat) is only 3 km from the centre.
features.notes: Width: Matton et al. 2005 and the 2008 thesis give about 50 m (outer) and 20 m (inner); the 2024 paper gives 70 m and 30 m. The map shows the ring as a dashed line where the dyke is hidden under sand, so some of the line is inferred from magnetic data.

features.label: Central breccia (dark grey on the map)
features.who: Matton, Jébrak and Lee
features.what: The core of broken, silica-cemented rock at the centre of the dome.
features.result: A hot-water karst collapse breccia; its internal sediment gave an argon age of 98.2 +/- 2.6 million years.

position.detail: Figure 1 of Abdeina et al. 2024 (CC BY). Control points: its printed graticule lines, one every 0.04 degrees (2 min 24 s) both ways, found at x = 242, 548, 855, 1160, 1467, 1772 px and y = 164, 491, 819, 1147, 1475 px of the 1896 x 2268 px figure, taken as lon -11.48 to -11.28 W and lat 21.20 to 21.04 N. The printed 2.5 km scale bar (183 px) gives the same scale as the grid (73.8 px/km). The corner labels are not on grid lines, so the grid lines were numbered by hand; the numbering was checked against the 30 m elevation model (south-west salt flat within 0.2 km) and ring traces. Envelope of the dark grey "Richat Guelb, Breccia" colour in the map, 6 degree steps around its centroid. The map draws the breccia in patches; the envelope joins them and covers about 14 km2, wider than the 3 km diameter in the text.

features.evidence: The centre of the depression is occupied by a breccia 3 km in diameter and up to 40 m thick.
features.notes: Treat this as the rough area of the mapped breccia, not its edge. Matton 2005: "The center of the Richat structure is occupied by a breccia body ~3 km in diameter and at least 40 m thick."

features.label: Kimberlite body under the north rim
features.who: Ashton Mining (trench); Matton and Jébrak; Abdeina and others
features.what: A kimberlite plug and sills in the north, no longer visible at the surface; the map outlines them as a buried body.
features.result: Dated by the mining company to about 99 million years (method and error not published).

position.detail: Figure 1 of Abdeina et al. 2024 (CC BY). Control points: its printed graticule lines, one every 0.04 degrees (2 min 24 s) both ways, found at x = 242, 548, 855, 1160, 1467, 1772 px and y = 164, 491, 819, 1147, 1475 px of the 1896 x 2268 px figure, taken as lon -11.48 to -11.28 W and lat 21.20 to 21.04 N. The printed 2.5 km scale bar (183 px) gives the same scale as the grid (73.8 px/km). The corner labels are not on grid lines, so the grid lines were numbered by hand; the numbering was checked against the 30 m elevation model (south-west salt flat within 0.2 km) and ring traces. Red dashed ellipse labelled "Veria Taleb" in the legend as "Kimberlite sub-surface", 10 degree steps.

features.evidence: Kimberlitic rocks described from a trench made by Ashton Mining in the northern part of the Richat Structure
features.notes: The 2024 paper adds that the presence at shallow depth "has been recently confirmed by magnetic records". The 99 Ma age is an unpublished company result quoted in Matton and Jébrak 2014 (read here through the thesis and the 2024 paper; the 2014 paper itself is paywalled and was not read).

features.label: Salt flat in the south-west crater
features.who: Matton and Jébrak
features.what: A flat of salt crust at the foot of the south-west volcanic crater, 2.5 km across in the thesis.
features.result: The crater is the remains of a small volcanic explosion pit (maar), younger than the dome.

position.detail: Figure 1 of Abdeina et al. 2024 (CC BY). Control points: its printed graticule lines, one every 0.04 degrees (2 min 24 s) both ways, found at x = 242, 548, 855, 1160, 1467, 1772 px and y = 164, 491, 819, 1147, 1475 px of the 1896 x 2268 px figure, taken as lon -11.48 to -11.28 W and lat 21.20 to 21.04 N. The printed 2.5 km scale bar (183 px) gives the same scale as the grid (73.8 px/km). The corner labels are not on grid lines, so the grid lines were numbered by hand; the numbering was checked against the 30 m elevation model (south-west salt flat within 0.2 km) and ring traces. White "Sabkha" fill south-west of the breccia, 10 degree steps. Its centroid is within 0.2 km of the flattest ground found independently in the 30 m elevation model.

features.evidence: a ~2.5 km diameter volcanic crater that crosscuts the inner basaltic ring dike, forming a circular depression filled by a sebkha.
features.notes: The salt flat on the map covers about 1.8 km2, smaller than the whole 2.5 km crater. Thesis text read; the crater circle in its figure 2 has no graticule.

features.who: Matton and Jébrak; Abdeina and others
features.what: A narrow sheet of carbonate-rich igneous rock cutting the ring strata, about 1.5 km long on the map.
features.result: Fission tracks in apatite from carbonatite (one neck and two dykes, Poupeau and others 1996) gave 99 +/- 5 million years.

position.detail: Figure 1 of Abdeina et al. 2024 (CC BY). Red line on the map, end points of its main axis. The map draws dykes wider than they are (they are 0.3-1.5 m thick).

features.evidence: Most of them occurred in the southern half of the structure.
features.notes: Ten of the ~40 red lines on the map are shown. The paper counts more than 60 dykes; the map length is a drawn length, Matton says they are about 300 m long.

measurements.what: Diameter of the whole domed structure
measurements.plato_value: Rings and central island together 27 stades across (Critias 115e-116a: 5 + 2 x (1+2+2+3+3)); about 5.0 km at 185 m a stade
measurements.evidence: a large dome at least 40 km in diameter

measurements.what: Distance from the centre to the outer rim ridge on its east and south arc
measurements.plato_value: Outer wall 50 stades beyond the largest ring, 127 stades across in all (our sum: 27 + 2 x 50); about 23.5 km at 185 m
measurements.evidence: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m), traced by this lane: outer rim ridge 21,540 to 24,180 m from the fitted centre over azimuth 45 to 230 degrees

measurements.what: Diameter of the third ridge ring (traced)
measurements.plato_value: 27 stades across, about 5.0 km (4.3 to 5.6 km for stades of 157.5 to 209 m)
measurements.evidence: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m), traced by this lane: mean radius 9,928 m (8,790 to 11,400 m)

measurements.what: Diameter of the second ridge ring (traced)
measurements.evidence: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m), traced by this lane: mean radius 6,591 m (5,910 to 7,140 m)

measurements.what: Diameter of the innermost ridge ring (traced)
measurements.plato_value: The central island is 5 stades across (Critias 116a), about 0.9 km at 185 m
measurements.evidence: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m), traced by this lane: mean radius 2,976 m (2,190 to 3,720 m)

measurements.what: Distance between neighbouring ridge crests (ring 1 to 2, then 2 to 3)
measurements.plato_value: Rings are 1 to 3 stades wide, at most about 0.56 km
measurements.evidence: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m), traced by this lane: mean radii 2,976 m, 6,591 m, 9,928 m

measurements.plato_value: The island with the palace is 5 stades across, about 0.9 km
measurements.evidence: a breccia body ~3 km in diameter and at least 40 m thick

measurements.what: Distance of the two gabbro rings from the centre
measurements.evidence: The ca. 70 m-wide outer ring (Tin Jouker) is located 7–8 km from the centre, while the 30 m-wide inner one (Guelb Richat) is only 3 km from the centre.

measurements.what: Shape: shorter axis divided by longer axis, for the central depression and for the whole structure
measurements.plato_value: Each ring has its circumference "equidistant every way from the centre" (Critias 113d), a true circle
measurements.evidence: give values ranging from 0.87-0.88 for both the central depression

measurements.what: Dip of the layers away from the centre (the rings are rock ridges, not water channels)
measurements.plato_value: Three rings of water and two of land (Critias 113d)
measurements.evidence: Erosion has created circular cuestas represented by three nested rings dipping outward from the structure.

measurements.what: Height of the structure centre above today's sea
measurements.plato_value: A canal 50 stades long runs from the sea to the outer ring, so the rings sit at sea level
measurements.evidence: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m) smoothed elevation at the fitted centre: 419 m (raw 419 m); Wikidata Q744591 gives 423 metre

measurements.what: Height of the ring ridge crests above today's sea
measurements.unit: m (mean 421, 465, 445 for rings 1 to 3; range 387 to 486)
measurements.evidence: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m), traced crest lines: ring 1 mean 421 m, ring 2 465 m, ring 3 445 m

measurements.what: Distance from the centre to the nearest Atlantic sea cell today
measurements.plato_value: Sea to outermost ring 50 stades, about 9 km at 185 m
measurements.evidence: GMRT GridServer, topo layer, about 1 km cells, ocean-connected cells at or below 0 m: nearest to 21.1185 N, 11.3975 W is at 20.236 N, 16.194 W; due west 16.783 W

measurements.what: Distance to the Atlantic when the sea stood about 125 m lower (last ice age low)
measurements.plato_value: Sea to outermost ring 50 stades, about 9 km at 185 m
measurements.evidence: GMRT GridServer, topo layer: nearest ocean cell at or below -125 m is at 19.647 N, 16.985 W; due west 17.521 W. Sea level then: "about 125 meters (410 ft) lower than today" (USGS, quoted by Wikipedia, Last Glacial Maximum)

measurements.what: Age of the carbonatite dykes (fission tracks in apatite)
measurements.plato_value: 9,000 years before the priest spoke to Solon (Timaeus 23e), about 9600 BCE
measurements.evidence: Fission-track dating of apatite in the carbonatite yielded a Mid-Cretaceous age (99 ± 5 Ma; Poupeau et al., 1996).

measurements.what: Age of the hot-water sediment in the central breccia (argon, K-feldspar)
Age of the two gabbro rings (modelled, no robust age)
measurements.evidence: Although no robust age was obtained, numerical modelling of our results suggests that the gabbros were intruded between 230 and 200 Ma.

measurements.what: The span the 2018 video gave for Atlantis: 127 stades converted to km
measurements.unit: km (20.0 to 26.5 for stades of 157.5 to 209 m)
measurements.plato_value: 27 + 2 x 50 = 127 stades is the whole city inside its outer wall (our sum from Critias 115e-117e); the rings themselves are 27
measurements.evidence: Atlantis was supposedly 127 stadia, or 23 kilometers (14 miles) across, which matches a portion of the Richat.

story.line: From 2008, writers and a film said the Richat's rings are Plato's rings of land and water, with the city at the centre.
A 2018 video added numbers: Atlantis 127 stades or about 23.5 km across, mountains to the north, rivers and a flood from the sea.
Geologists had first read the circle as a meteorite crater; fieldwork in the 1960s found no shock rock and the idea was dropped.
The rings are rock ridges, 6, 13 and 20 km across, in a dome over 40 km wide that stands about 420 m above the sea.
Matton and colleagues mapped a 3 km breccia core and dated it, and the carbonate dykes, to about 99 million years ago.
In 2024 six gabbro samples were analysed and two dated by argon: no sharp age, but about 230 to 200 million years, not 99.
Stone tool makers visited long ago: tools lie along the wadis of the outer ring, but no house, wall or canal has been reported.

not_located.what: The rings and city as the proposers drew them (Corsetti 2018 video; Alexander and Rosen film; Sarantitis)
not_located.why: The video and film overlay Plato's rings on satellite images but publish no coordinates, centre or scale. Only the diameter number (127 stades, 23.5 km) is stated, so no outline can be drawn from them. The scene can draw Plato's rings at true scale from plato.json around the structure centre and say so.

not_located.what: Acheulean and pre-Acheulean tool sites (Sao, Giresse and others 2008; Monod)
not_located.why: Site positions are in the 2008 paper (L'Anthropologie 112), which is paywalled and was not read. Wikipedia says only that the main sites lie "along the northwest of the outer ring" between wadis Akerdil and Bamouéré. No coordinates found in any open source.

not_located.what: Sample point of the 98.2 Ma K-feldspar sediment in the breccia (Matton et al. 2005)
not_located.why: The paper gives no coordinates; it only says the sediment fills cavities in the centre of the breccia body.

not_located.what: Dietz, Fudali and Cassidy 1969 sample and thin-section sites (no-impact check)
not_located.why: The paper (GSA Bulletin 80:1367) was not open; no abstract or coordinates were found.

not_located.what: Rivers and valley the 2018 video says flow from northern mountains, and a flood channel
not_located.why: No map or coordinates published; the video itself was not fetched. Critics describe a sand drift to the south-west, not a river.
The escarpment north and west of the structure shows in the elevation model but our ridge filter cannot separate it from the outer ring, so no outline was kept.

not_located.what: Semsiyat Dome, a smaller circular structure about 50 km west-south-west
not_located.why: Named by Atlantipedia and Dietz 1969; not part of the Richat claims, no position fetched.

handoffs.what: Draw Plato's rings (5 stades island; water 1, 2, 3; land 2, 3; 27 stades across; wall at 127) at true scale on this centre, with a switch for stade length 157.5 to 209 m. Our measured ridge rings are 6, 13 and 20 km across.
Use copernicus-dem-aws hillshade and eox-s2cloudless-2016 for the ring ridges; macrostrat-geology for rock units.
Add the 2024 Lithos paper (Abdeina et al.) to searches.json: first argon age on the Richat gabbros, 230 to 200 Ma modelled, sills not ring dykes. It is CC BY and open.
The 2024 Lithos paper is open (CC BY): it could be stored as text. So could the Matton 2008 thesis (UQAM open copy, 172 pages, French and English).

not_verified: The 2018 video itself was not watched; every claim is as reported by Colavito (14 Sept 2018), Ancient Origins and Novella (19 Nov 2018). Hypotheses.json dates the video to Nov 2018; Colavito's post shows it was circulating by 14 Sept 2018.
The "flood from the east" lead: no source says this. Novella says the video has the Atlantic flooding the Sahara and an opening to the south-west.

Matton and Jébrak 2014 (J. African Earth Sci. 97:109-124, doi:10.1016/j.jafrearsci.2014.04.006) is paywalled and was not read. Its content is known here only through Matton's open 2008 thesis (which holds the same paper as a chapter in draft), the 2024 Lithos paper and Wikipedia.
Dietz et al. 1969: no text or abstract fetched. That it argued "not astroblemes" and that coesite was barite is from Wikipedia and Matton et al. 2005 (which cite it), not from the paper.
Sao, Giresse et al. 2008: Crossref and OpenAlex have no abstract. The statement about sites along the wadis of the outer ring is from Wikipedia, which cites it.
Giuliani's book (2008, self-published) and Alexander and Rosen's 2006 idea and late-2008 visit are from Atlantipedia (a sceptical reference site) and the film's own site; their text was not seen.

Seven features on the 2024 map (Fig. 1) were located by the printed graticule, but the corner labels do not sit on grid lines, so grid lines were numbered by hand. Check: the independent 30 m elevation model puts the flattest ground in the south-west crater within 0.2 km of the map's salt flat. Against that, the map's well "Hassi Thiba" plots 2.1 km east of the OSM/GNS position (21.0041 N, 11.4309 W); one of the two is off.
Elevation: the Copernicus model is a surface model; on bare rock this is the ground. OSM tags the peak at 485 m; the model gives up to about 515 m on ring crests and 630 m in the 50 km box.
Wikipedia says the breccia covers "an area that is at least 30 kilometres in diameter" in one sentence, against 3 km in the sources read; treated as a typo.
